main_text.p: occurrunt termini, qui pertinent ad philosophiam theoreticam & practicam. In veteri Testamento occurrunt terminiMetaphysici,quales sunt τὸ ὄν[?],ens, Exod.6.Apoc.1.Bonum,Gen.1. occurrunt physici, ut cœlum, terra, aqua, ignis, aër, arbores, animalia bruta,meteora, gemmæ,metalla & similes,in libris Mosis,in libro Jobi,in Psalmis, aliisq; veteris instrumenti libris: occurrunt geographici, ut paradisus,itinera Patriarcharum, topographiæ, mare rubrum: occurrunt Astronomici, ut Orion, Arcturus, Pleiades,Sol,Luna: occurrunt hinc inde Chronologici, ut sunt septimanæ Danielis: occurrunt in N.T. parabolæ, navigatio Pauli, itinera Apostolorum: occurrunt præcepta Ethica, de liberalitate, de veracitate,de temperantiâ: occurrunt canones œconomici, de marito,uxore,liberis,servis: occurrunt deniq; politici de regno,de rege,subditis, legibus, bello, armis, similibusq; materiis: ut videre est in libris scriptuʀ historicis,itemq; didacticis, nominatim in libris Regum,Chronicorum,Nehemiæ,Ezræ, in Proverbiis & Ecclesiastę Solomonis, in epistolis Apostolorum. Vide hâc de re eruditissimas tractationes, Pici Comitis Mirandulæ heptalogum admirandum: Benedicti Ariæ Montani Jofephum, de arcano sermone; ejusdem Jeremiam, de actione; ejusdem librum de idiotismis linguæ sanctæ; ejusdem Phaleg, de gentium regionibus: ejusdem deniq; Nehemiam, de urbe sanctâ, & Danielem,de temporibus. Item partem 1.& 2. clavis sacræ scripturæ Flacci Illyrici, ubi agit de situ Cananæ, de necessitate cognitionis, de isto SS. literarum, de tropis & schematis

page.notes: The lines are cut off at the right edge of this part; the word fragments are as far as they are visible. The rest of the lines continue in the other part of the page. The line "de tropis & schematis" ends the page; "S. lite-" is the catchword. Greek "τὸ ὄν" is hard to read and is marked [?]. Fragments at the far left edge of the scan belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed. Show-through at the right edge is ignored. Printed forms kept: "Jofephum", "Jobi", "aliisq;", "deniq;", "scriptuʀ" (long-s and s forms as printed where they are abbreviations or ligatures).
